locations.name: The Flatiron Building
locations.factShort: The Flatiron Building (originally the Fuller Building) is a 22-story, 307-foot-tall steel-framed triangular building at 175 Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron District neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. Designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P. Dinkelberg, it opened in 1902.

locations.name: The Brooklyn Museum
locations.factShort: The Brooklyn Museum is an art museum in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. At 560,000 square feet, the museum is New York City's second largest and contains an art collection with around 500,000 objects.

locations.name: Citi Field
locations.factShort: Citi Field is a baseball stadium located in Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, in the borough of Queens, New York City, United States. Opened in 2009, Citi Field is the home of Major League Baseball's New York Mets.

locations.name: Woodlawn Cemetery
locations.factShort: Woodlawn Cemetery is one of the largest cemeteries in New York City and a designated National Historic Landmark. Located south of Woodlawn Heights, Bronx, it has the character of a rural cemetery. It is notable in part as the final resting place of some well-known figures.

locations.name: The Conference House
locations.factShort: Conference House (also known as Billop House) is a stone house in the Tottenville neighborhood of Staten Island in New York City.
